records.source: Καὶ εἶδον ἐκ τῆς θαλάσσης θηρίον ἀναβαῖνον, ἔχον κέρατα δέκα καὶ κεφαλὰς ἑπτά, καὶ ἐπὶ τῶν κεράτων αὐτοῦ δέκα διαδήματα, καὶ ἐπὶ τὰς κεφαλὰς αὐτοῦ ὀνόματα βλασφημίας.
records.gloss: And I saw out of the sea a beast coming up, having horns ten and heads seven, and on the horns of it ten diadems, and on the heads of it names of blasphemy.
pieces: Then I saw a beast rising out of the sea. It had ten horns and seven heads, ten royal crowns on its horns, and on its heads names that blasphemed God.

L.1: And I saw a beast coming up out of the sea, having ten horns and seven heads, and on its horns ten royal crowns, and on its heads names of blasphemy.

R.1: Then I saw a beast coming up out of the sea. It had ten horns and seven heads. There was a king's crown on each horn. On each head was a name that insulted God.

decisions.choice: a beast from the sea: Daniel 7
decisions.reason: Daniel saw four great beasts come up out of the sea, the fourth with ten horns, and was told that they are kingdoms (Daniel 7:2-8, 17, 23-24). The sea stood for the chaotic powers opposed to God. This beast has the dragon's heads and horns (12:3): it is his agent.

decisions.choice: the beast: a power that opposes God and demands worship
alternatives: the Roman Empire and its emperors in John's day
a recurring pattern of state power set against God
a final ruler at the end of history
decisions.reason: Many features point to Rome as John's readers knew it: emperors who claimed divine titles, worship of the emperor in the cities of Asia, and the city on seven hills (17:9). Many readers also see in the beast a pattern that recurs wherever earthly power claims what belongs to God, and some a final figure at the end. The text uses symbols and does not name it.

decisions.choice: names of blasphemy: titles that claim divine honor
decisions.reason: The beast bears names that insult God by claiming what is his. Roman emperors were given titles such as "divine", "son of god" and "lord".

decisions.choice: it, its: the beast
decisions.reason: θηρίον is neuter, and every level calls the beast "it".

records.heading: The beast from the sea

records.source: καὶ τὸ θηρίον ὃ εἶδον ἦν ὅμοιον παρδάλει, καὶ οἱ πόδες αὐτοῦ ὡς ἄρκου, καὶ τὸ στόμα αὐτοῦ ὡς στόμα λέοντος.
records.gloss: And the beast which I saw was like to a leopard, and the feet of it as of a bear, and the mouth of it as mouth of a lion.
pieces: The beast I saw was like a leopard; its feet were like a bear's, and its mouth like the mouth of a lion.

L.2: And the beast that I saw was like a leopard, and its feet [were] like a bear's, and its mouth like a lion's mouth.

R.2: The beast looked like a leopard. But it had feet like a bear and a mouth like a lion.

decisions.choice: leopard, bear and lion: Daniel's beasts in one
decisions.reason: Daniel's first three beasts were like a lion, a bear and a leopard (Daniel 7:4-6). John's beast combines them, in reverse order: it gathers up all the empires that went before.

records.source: καὶ ἔδωκεν αὐτῷ ὁ δράκων τὴν δύναμιν αὐτοῦ καὶ τὸν θρόνον αὐτοῦ καὶ ἐξουσίαν μεγάλην.
records.gloss: And gave to it the dragon the power of him and the throne of him and authority great.
pieces: The dragon handed over to it his power, his throne, and great authority.

L.2: And the dragon gave it his power and his throne and great authority.

R.2: The dragon gave the beast his own power, his throne, and great authority.

decisions.choice: the dragon's gift: a parody of the Father's gift to the Son
decisions.reason: The devil claimed to have the authority of the world's kingdoms to give (Luke 4:5-6). As the Father gives authority to the Son (2:27-28; 5:7), the dragon gives his throne to the beast.

records.source: καὶ μίαν ἐκ τῶν κεφαλῶν αὐτοῦ ὡς ἐσφαγμένην εἰς θάνατον, καὶ ἡ πληγὴ τοῦ θανάτου αὐτοῦ ἐθεραπεύθη.
records.gloss: And one of the heads of it as having been slaughtered to death, and the wound of the death of it was healed.
pieces: One of its heads looked as though it had been slaughtered and killed, but its deadly wound had been healed.

L.3: And one of its heads [was] as though slaughtered to death, and its death-wound was healed.

R.3: One of the beast's heads looked as if it had been killed. But the deadly wound had healed.

decisions.choice: as though slaughtered, and healed: a parody of the Lamb
decisions.reason: ὡς ἐσφαγμένην are the words used of the Lamb, "as though slaughtered" (5:6). The beast imitates the death and resurrection of Christ, to win the world's wonder (13:3-4, 14).

decisions.choice: a wounded head that recovers: perhaps the legend of Nero's return
decisions.reason: After the emperor Nero died by his own hand in AD 68, rumors spread that he was alive and would return, and pretenders arose (Tacitus, Histories 2.8; Suetonius, Nero 57). Some see that legend behind the healed head; others see the recovery of the empire after the civil wars of AD 68-69. The text does not say.

records.source: καὶ ἐθαυμάσθη ὅλη ἡ γῆ ὀπίσω τοῦ θηρίου, καὶ προσεκύνησαν τῷ δράκοντι ὅτι ἔδωκεν τὴν ἐξουσίαν τῷ θηρίῳ, καὶ προσεκύνησαν τῷ θηρίῳ λέγοντες· Τίς ὅμοιος τῷ θηρίῳ, καὶ τίς δύναται πολεμῆσαι μετ’ αὐτοῦ;
records.gloss: And marveled whole the earth after the beast, \v 4 and they worshiped the dragon because he gave the authority to the beast, and they worshiped the beast saying: Who [is] like to the beast, and who is able to make war with it?
pieces: In amazement the whole earth went after the beast.
They worshiped the dragon, since he had given his authority to the beast, and they worshiped the beast as well, saying, "Who is equal to the beast? Who could fight a war against it?"

L.3: And the whole earth marveled [and followed] after the beast,
L.4: and they worshiped the dragon because he had given his authority to the beast, and they worshiped the beast, saying, "Who is like the beast, and who can make war with it?"

R.3: The whole world was amazed and followed the beast.
R.4: People worshiped the dragon because he had given his power to the beast. They also worshiped the beast. They said, "Who is as great as the beast? Who can fight against it?"

decisions.choice: Who is like the beast? A parody of praise to God
decisions.reason: Israel sang, "Who is like you, O LORD, among the gods?" (Exodus 15:11; compare Psalm 89:7-9). The name Michael (12:7) means "Who is like God?" The world gives the beast the praise that belongs to God.

decisions.choice: marveled after the beast: wondered and followed
decisions.reason: "Marveled after" packs two ideas: they were amazed and went after it as followers.

records.source: Καὶ ἐδόθη αὐτῷ στόμα λαλοῦν μεγάλα καὶ βλασφημίας, καὶ ἐδόθη αὐτῷ ἐξουσία ποιῆσαι μῆνας τεσσεράκοντα δύο.
records.gloss: And was given to it a mouth speaking great things and blasphemies, and was given to it authority to act months forty-two.
pieces: It was allowed a mouth that spoke boastful words and blasphemies, and it was given authority to act for forty-two months.

L.5: And a mouth was given to it speaking great things and blasphemies, and authority was given to it to act for forty-two months.

R.5: The beast was allowed to say proud things and to insult God. It was given power to do what it wanted for forty-two months.

decisions.choice: a mouth speaking great things: Daniel's little horn
decisions.reason: Daniel's little horn had "a mouth speaking great things" and spoke words against the Most High; the saints were given into its hand for a time, times and half a time (Daniel 7:8, 20, 25). Forty-two months is the same span (11:2; 12:6, 14).

decisions.choice: was given: within God's limits
decisions.reason: The repeated "was given" (13:5, 7, 14, 15) shows that the beast acts only for the time and within the bounds God allows.

records.source: καὶ ἤνοιξε τὸ στόμα αὐτοῦ εἰς βλασφημίας πρὸς τὸν θεόν, βλασφημῆσαι τὸ ὄνομα αὐτοῦ καὶ τὴν σκηνὴν αὐτοῦ, τοὺς ἐν τῷ οὐρανῷ σκηνοῦντας.
records.gloss: And it opened the mouth of it for blasphemies toward the God, to blaspheme the name of him and the tent of him, those in the heaven dwelling.
pieces: Its mouth opened in blasphemies against God, insulting {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} name and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} dwelling, those whose home is in heaven.

L.6: And it opened its mouth in blasphemies against God, to blaspheme {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} name and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} dwelling, those who dwell in heaven.

R.6: It began to say insulting things against God. It insulted God's name and the place where {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} lives, and everyone who lives in heaven.

decisions.choice: his dwelling, those who dwell in heaven
alternatives: his dwelling and those who dwell in heaven, as two objects
decisions.reason: σκηνὴν is God's tent or dwelling (compare 21:3). The phrase that follows most likely explains it: God's dwelling is his people with him in heaven. Some manuscripts add "and", making them two objects.

records.source: καὶ ἐδόθη αὐτῷ ποιῆσαι πόλεμον μετὰ τῶν ἁγίων καὶ νικῆσαι αὐτούς, καὶ ἐδόθη αὐτῷ ἐξουσία ἐπὶ πᾶσαν φυλὴν καὶ λαὸν καὶ γλῶσσαν καὶ ἔθνος.
records.gloss: And it was given to it to make war with the saints and to overcome them, and was given to it authority over every tribe and people and tongue and nation.
pieces: It was allowed to make war on God's holy people and to overcome them; and authority was given to it over every tribe and people and language and nation.

L.7: And it was allowed to make war with the saints and to overcome them, and authority was given to it over every tribe and people and language and nation.

R.7: It was allowed to fight against God's people and to defeat them. It was given power over every tribe, people, language, and nation.

decisions.choice: war on the saints: Daniel 7:21
decisions.reason: Daniel's horn "made war with the saints and prevailed over them" until God gave judgment (Daniel 7:21-22). νικῆσαι is the "overcome" of the letters: the beast seems to win, but the saints overcome by faithful witness (12:11; 15:2).

decisions.choice: the first clause is present
alternatives: the clause "it was allowed to make war with the saints and to overcome them" is missing
decisions.reason: Some early manuscripts leave out the first clause, perhaps by an accidental skip from one "and it was given" to the next. The SBLGNT includes it, and the translation follows it. Reviewers should check this against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: saints (L); God's holy people (B); God's people (R)
decisions.reason: As in 5:8.

records.source: καὶ προσκυνήσουσιν αὐτὸν πάντες οἱ κατοικοῦντες ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς, οὗ οὐ γέγραπται τὸ ὄνομα αὐτοῦ ἐν τῷ βιβλίῳ τῆς ζωῆς τοῦ ἀρνίου τοῦ ἐσφαγμένου ἀπὸ καταβολῆς κόσμου.
records.gloss: And will worship it all those dwelling on the earth, of whom not has been written the name of him in the book of the life of the Lamb the [one] having been slaughtered from foundation of world.
pieces: All who live on the earth will worship it, everyone whose name has not been written, since the world was founded, in the book of life belonging to the Lamb who was slaughtered.

L.8: And all who live on the earth will worship it, everyone whose name has not been written from the foundation of the world in the book of life of the Lamb who was slaughtered.

R.8: All the people on earth will worship the beast. These are the people whose names were not written in the book of life before the world was made. The book of life belongs to the Lamb who was killed.

decisions.choice: "from the foundation of the world" goes with "written"
alternatives: it goes with "slaughtered": the Lamb slaughtered from the foundation of the world
decisions.reason: The phrase stands at the end of the sentence, after "the Lamb who was slaughtered", and could describe the Lamb's death as planned from before creation (compare 1 Peter 1:19-20). But Revelation 17:8 uses the same phrase of names "not written in the book of life from the foundation of the world", which favors taking it with "written" here too. The words of the sentence allow both.

decisions.choice: the book of life of the Lamb
decisions.reason: See the note on 3:5. The book belongs to the Lamb who was slaughtered: those written in it are those he redeemed (5:9).

decisions.choice: the phrase placed by "written" (L, B, R)
decisions.reason: To follow the punctuation decision (m1), every level puts "from the foundation of the world" next to "written", where English can show what it modifies.

records.source: Εἴ τις ἔχει οὖς ἀκουσάτω.
records.gloss: If anyone has an ear, let him hear.
pieces: If anyone has ears, let {{gender:them|him}} listen.

L.9: If anyone has an ear, let {{gender:that person|him}} hear.

R.9: Anyone who can hear should listen carefully.

decisions.choice: the call of the seven letters
decisions.reason: The call that closed each letter (2:7) returns, now without "what the Spirit says to the churches": what follows is a warning for every hearer.

records.source: εἴ τις εἰς αἰχμαλωσίαν, εἰς αἰχμαλωσίαν ὑπάγει· εἴ τις ἐν μαχαίρῃ ἀποκτανθῆναι αὐτὸν ἐν μαχαίρῃ ἀποκτανθῆναι.
records.gloss: If anyone into captivity, into captivity he goes; if anyone with sword to be killed, him with sword to be killed.
pieces: Whoever is bound for captivity goes into captivity; whoever is to die by the sword must die by the sword.

L.10: If anyone [is] for captivity, into captivity {{gender:that person|he}} goes; if anyone [is] to be killed with the sword, with the sword {{gender:that person|he}} [is] to be killed.

R.10: Some people will be taken away as prisoners. That is what will happen to them. Some people will be killed with swords. That is what will happen to them.

decisions.choice: captivity and the sword: Jeremiah 15:2
decisions.reason: God told Jeremiah: "Those for death, to death; those for the sword, to the sword; those for famine, to famine; those for captivity, to captivity" (Jeremiah 15:2; 43:11). Believers must accept what is coming to them without escaping into compromise.

decisions.choice: if anyone is to be killed by the sword, by the sword they must be killed
alternatives: if anyone kills with the sword, by the sword they must be killed
decisions.reason: The SBLGNT reads the passive, "to be killed", following Jeremiah. Other manuscripts read "if anyone kills with the sword", which makes it a warning against using violence, as in Matthew 26:52. The translation follows the SBLGNT. Reviewers should check this against the SBLGNT apparatus.

records.source: ὧδέ ἐστιν ἡ ὑπομονὴ καὶ ἡ πίστις τῶν ἁγίων.
records.gloss: Here is the endurance and the faith of the saints.
pieces: Here is where God's holy people need endurance and faith.

L.10: Here is the endurance and the faith of the saints.

R.10: This is why God's people must keep going and keep their faith.

decisions.choice: faith: trust that holds firm, faithfulness
decisions.reason: πίστις can mean faith or faithfulness. Beside "endurance" it means the trust that keeps believers faithful under pressure (compare 14:12).

decisions.choice: here: in this situation
decisions.reason: "Here" points to the beast's power just described: this is where the saints' endurance and faith are needed and shown.

decisions.choice: saints (L); God's holy people (B); God's people (R)
decisions.reason: As in 5:8.

records.source: Καὶ εἶδον ἄλλο θηρίον ἀναβαῖνον ἐκ τῆς γῆς, καὶ εἶχεν κέρατα δύο ὅμοια ἀρνίῳ, καὶ ἐλάλει ὡς δράκων.
records.gloss: And I saw another beast coming up out of the earth, and it had horns two like to a lamb, and it was speaking as a dragon.
pieces: I saw yet another beast coming up from the land. Its two horns were like a lamb's, yet its voice was the voice of a dragon.

L.11: And I saw another beast coming up out of the earth, and it had two horns like a lamb, and it spoke like a dragon.

R.11: Then I saw another beast coming up out of the ground. It had two horns like a lamb. But it talked like a dragon.

decisions.choice: the second beast: the false prophet
decisions.reason: Later this beast is called "the false prophet" (16:13; 19:20). It looks harmless, like a lamb, but speaks for the dragon. Jesus warned of false prophets who come in sheep's clothing (Matthew 7:15). It may stand for the religious and civic powers that promoted the worship of the emperor in Asia.

decisions.choice: out of the earth: from the land, in contrast to the sea
decisions.reason: γῆς can mean earth or land. The first beast came from the sea, this one from the land; together they cover the world.

records.heading: The beast from the earth

records.source: καὶ τὴν ἐξουσίαν τοῦ πρώτου θηρίου πᾶσαν ποιεῖ ἐνώπιον αὐτοῦ.
records.gloss: And the authority of the first beast all it exercises before it.
pieces: All the authority of the first beast it puts to use, acting in its presence.

L.12: And it exercises all the authority of the first beast in its presence.

R.12: It used all the power of the first beast, working for it.

decisions.choice: before it: in its presence, on its behalf
decisions.reason: ἐνώπιον means "in front of". The second beast acts as the first beast's servant and representative.

records.source: καὶ ποιεῖ τὴν γῆν καὶ τοὺς ἐν αὐτῇ κατοικοῦντας ἵνα προσκυνήσουσιν τὸ θηρίον τὸ πρῶτον, οὗ ἐθεραπεύθη ἡ πληγὴ τοῦ θανάτου αὐτοῦ.
records.gloss: And it makes the earth and those in it dwelling that they will worship the beast the first, of whom was healed the wound of the death of it.
pieces: It forces the earth and its people to worship the first beast, whose deadly wound was healed.

L.12: And it makes the earth and those who live in it worship the first beast, whose deadly wound was healed.

R.12: It made everyone on earth worship the first beast, the one whose deadly wound had healed.

decisions.choice: a false religion that points to the beast
decisions.reason: The second beast does for the first what the Spirit does for Christ: it draws worship to him. Revelation exposes the worship of earthly power as idolatry.

records.source: καὶ ποιεῖ σημεῖα μεγάλα, ἵνα καὶ πῦρ ποιῇ ἐκ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ καταβαίνειν εἰς τὴν γῆν ἐνώπιον τῶν ἀνθρώπων.
records.gloss: And it does signs great, so that even fire it makes out of the heaven to come down to the earth before the men.
pieces: It performs great signs, even bringing fire down from the sky to the earth in front of everyone.

L.13: And it performs great signs, so that it even makes fire come down from heaven to the earth in the sight of {{gender:people|men}}.

R.13: It did great miracles, called signs. It even made fire come down from the sky to the earth while people watched.

decisions.choice: fire from heaven: a counterfeit of Elijah
decisions.reason: Elijah called down fire from heaven to show that the LORD is God (1 Kings 18:38), and the two witnesses have fire from their mouths (11:5). The second beast imitates the signs of God's prophets. Moses warned against prophets who give signs and lead to other gods (Deuteronomy 13:1-3), and Jesus and Paul warned of false signs (Mark 13:22; 2 Thessalonians 2:9).

decisions.choice: signs; miracles, called signs (R)
decisions.reason: Sign is a key term and stays. Readable adds what the signs were.

records.source: καὶ πλανᾷ τοὺς κατοικοῦντας ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς διὰ τὰ σημεῖα ἃ ἐδόθη αὐτῷ ποιῆσαι ἐνώπιον τοῦ θηρίου, λέγων τοῖς κατοικοῦσιν ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς ποιῆσαι εἰκόνα τῷ θηρίῳ, ὃς ἔχει τὴν πληγὴν τῆς μαχαίρης καὶ ἔζησεν.
records.gloss: And it deceives those dwelling on the earth because of the signs which were given to it to do before the beast, telling those dwelling on the earth to make an image to the beast, which has the wound of the sword and lived.
pieces: It leads astray the people of the earth with the signs it was allowed to do in the beast's presence, and it tells them to make an image for the beast that had the sword-wound and yet came back to life.

L.14: And it deceives those who live on the earth by the signs that it was allowed to perform in the presence of the beast, telling those who live on the earth to make an image for the beast that has the wound of the sword and came to life.

R.14: It fooled the people on earth with the signs it was allowed to do for the first beast. It told them to make a statue to honor the beast that had been wounded by a sword and yet lived.

decisions.choice: an image: a statue for worship
decisions.reason: Nebuchadnezzar set up a golden image and commanded all to worship it (Daniel 3). In the cities of Asia there were temples and statues of the emperors, where offerings were made.

decisions.choice: wounded and came to life: the beast's false resurrection
decisions.reason: ἔζησεν is the verb used of Christ, "who was dead and came to life" (2:8). The beast mimics the resurrection (13:3).

decisions.choice: image (L, B); statue (R)
decisions.reason: Readable uses the plain word for what was set up.

records.source: καὶ ἐδόθη αὐτῷ δοῦναι πνεῦμα τῇ εἰκόνι τοῦ θηρίου, ἵνα καὶ λαλήσῃ ἡ εἰκὼν τοῦ θηρίου καὶ ποιήσῃ ἵνα ὅσοι ἐὰν μὴ προσκυνήσωσιν τῇ εἰκόνι τοῦ θηρίου ἀποκτανθῶσιν.
records.gloss: And it was given to it to give breath to the image of the beast, so that also might speak the image of the beast and might cause that as many as if not would worship the image of the beast be killed.
pieces: It was permitted to give life-breath to the image of the beast, so that the image could even speak, and could have put to death all who refused to worship it.

L.15: And it was allowed to give breath to the image of the beast, so that the image of the beast would even speak and would cause as many as do not worship the image of the beast to be killed.

R.15: It was allowed to give breath to the statue of the beast, so that the statue could talk. The statue ordered that everyone who would not worship it must be killed.

decisions.choice: death for refusing to worship: Daniel 3
decisions.reason: Those who would not bow to Nebuchadnezzar's image were to be thrown into the furnace (Daniel 3:6). Pliny the Younger, governor of a neighboring province around AD 112, wrote that he executed Christians who would not offer wine and incense to the emperor's image.

decisions.choice: a speaking image
decisions.reason: πνεῦμα is breath or spirit. The second beast makes the image seem alive, a false likeness of God giving the breath of life (11:11). Ancient writers describe tricks that made statues seem to speak.

records.source: καὶ ποιεῖ πάντας, τοὺς μικροὺς καὶ τοὺς μεγάλους, καὶ τοὺς πλουσίους καὶ τοὺς πτωχούς, καὶ τοὺς ἐλευθέρους καὶ τοὺς δούλους, ἵνα δῶσιν αὐτοῖς χάραγμα ἐπὶ τῆς χειρὸς αὐτῶν τῆς δεξιᾶς ἢ ἐπὶ τὸ μέτωπον αὐτῶν, καὶ ἵνα μή τις δύνηται ἀγοράσαι ἢ πωλῆσαι εἰ μὴ ὁ ἔχων τὸ χάραγμα, τὸ ὄνομα τοῦ θηρίου ἢ τὸν ἀριθμὸν τοῦ ὀνόματος αὐτοῦ.
records.gloss: And it makes all, the small and the great, and the rich and the poor, and the free and the slaves, that they give them a mark on the hand of them the right or on the forehead of them, \v 17 and that not anyone may be able to buy or to sell except the [one] having the mark, the name of the beast or the number of the name of it.
pieces: It makes everyone, the lowly and the great, the rich and the poor, the free and the slave, take a mark on the right hand or on the forehead.
No one may buy or sell except those who have the mark: the name of the beast or the number that stands for its name.

L.16: And it causes all, the small and the great, and the rich and the poor, and the free and the slaves, to be given a mark on their right hand or on their forehead,
L.17: so that no one can buy or sell except the one who has the mark, the name of the beast or the number of its name.

R.16: It forced all people to have a mark put on their right hand or on their forehead. It did this to important and unimportant people, rich and poor, free people and slaves.
R.17: No one could buy or sell anything without this mark. The mark was the name of the beast or the number of its name.

decisions.choice: a mark: a brand or stamp of ownership, a counterfeit of God's seal
decisions.reason: χάραγμα was used of a brand on slaves or animals and of the imperial stamp on documents and coins. God's slaves are sealed on the forehead (7:3; 14:1); the beast's followers bear its mark. Whether it is a visible mark or a picture of allegiance, it shows whom a person belongs to.

decisions.choice: hand and forehead: a parody of God's words on the hand and between the eyes
decisions.reason: Israel was told to bind God's words "as a sign on your hand and as frontlets between your eyes" (Deuteronomy 6:8). The beast demands the same place for its mark: loyalty in deed and thought.

decisions.choice: no buying or selling: economic exclusion
decisions.reason: In the cities of Asia, trade guilds held feasts in honor of the gods and the emperor, and refusing to take part could cost believers their livelihood (compare 2:9, 2:20). The mark's power is economic as well as religious.

decisions.choice: slaves
decisions.reason: "Slave" at every level, as the style guide keeps it where slave is set against free.

records.source: ὧδε ἡ σοφία ἐστίν· ὁ ἔχων νοῦν ψηφισάτω τὸν ἀριθμὸν τοῦ θηρίου, ἀριθμὸς γὰρ ἀνθρώπου ἐστίν· καὶ ὁ ἀριθμὸς αὐτοῦ ἑξακόσιοι ἑξήκοντα ἕξ.
records.gloss: Here the wisdom is. The [one] having understanding let him count the number of the beast, for number of a man it is, and the number of it 666.
pieces: Here wisdom is needed. Whoever has understanding should count up the number of the beast, for it is a human number. Its number is 666.

L.18: Here is wisdom: let the one who has understanding calculate the number of the beast, for it is [the] number of a human, and its number [is] 666.

R.18: Here you need wisdom. If you are wise, you can figure out the number of the beast. It stands for a person. The number is 666.

decisions.choice: 666: a number that may spell a name
alternatives: the name of the emperor Nero, spelled in Hebrew letters
a number that falls short of seven, the number of completeness, three times over
a name that cannot now be known
decisions.reason: In Greek and Hebrew, letters were also numbers, and a name could be counted up. Spelled in Hebrew letters, the Greek title "Nero Caesar" adds up to 666, and a Latin spelling to 616 (see m2). Others take 666 as the number that falls short of seven at every point, the opposite of God's completeness. "The number of a man" can mean the number of a particular person or a human number. Many names have been proposed; John asks the reader for wisdom, not guessing.

The SBLGNT reads 666. A few early witnesses read 616, and Irenaeus, in the second century, knew of that reading and rejected it. The translation follows the SBLGNT. Reviewers should check this against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: 666 (numerals)
decisions.reason: The number is given in figures, as the style guide does for large numbers.
